title: Loss of Seat Power During Turnaround on Retrofitted Cabins — Request for a Higher Rated Supply
abstract: Operator asks for a higher rated in-seat power supply after the retrofitted cabin repeatedly drops passenger device charging on ground power during turnaround, generating cabin complaints and unnecessary technical log entries.

sections.request: Since we refitted our cabins with the new seat product, the in-seat power keeps dropping out on the ground. It happens during turnaround, almost always when we are on ground power with the packs running and the cabin crew are boarding. The seat sockets go dead in blocks, usually the rear third of the cabin first, and come back a few minutes later on their own. Cabin crew log it every time, so we now have a technical log entry on nearly every rotation on some aircraft, and our engineers cannot reproduce it at the gate because it clears itself. Passengers notice it because they are charging phones during boarding. We do not think this is a seat problem, we think the supply behind it is simply not big enough for the number of sockets we have fitted. We would like a properly rated supply so that we can close this out rather than keep writing it up.
sections.background: The cabin refit was completed across the sub-fleet during 2025. Before the refit each seat row had two sockets, after it every seat has one, which roughly doubles the connected load in the aft cabin. The dropouts started within weeks of the first aircraft coming out of the refit line and now affect eleven aircraft. Our dispatch reliability is not affected but the repeat technical log entries are, and two aircraft have been through a full harness continuity check for nothing. Our maintenance provider believes the supply is protecting itself rather than failing.
sections.expected_outcome: A supply and distribution standard that carries the full fitted socket count with margin on ground power, retrofittable during a normal night stop, and that lets us close the repeat technical log entries without a cabin re-configuration.

type_data.business_justification: Repeat technical log entries on eleven aircraft consume line engineering time on almost every rotation and undermine the commercial case for the cabin refit that the operator has just funded.
